_comment: IBM M&A history extracted from annual report filings. 'tier':'major' = deals >$500M or strategic significance. valueSource='filing' means the dollar figure was read directly from the report's Acquisitions & Divestitures note or cash flow statement; 'announced' means the figure comes from IBM's contemporaneous press release/8-K (also a primary IBM source, just not the annual report). All values in US$ millions.

deals.name: Dayton Scale Division → Hobart Manufacturing
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Sold the Dayton Scale Division to The Hobart Manufacturing Company in exchange for 100,000 shares of Hobart Class B capital stock. Net current assets transferred were $1,931,266.68 plus plant, equipment, patents and goodwill. Approved at a special stockholders meeting June 25 1934. Certain foreign assets of the division followed in 1936. Non-cash consideration: no dollar sale price disclosed.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1934 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Time Equipment Division → Simplex Time Recorder
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Announced Oct 24 1958, effective Dec 1 1958. Sold the domestic Time Equipment Division to Simplex Time Recorder Company (Gardner MA) to concentrate on product divisions contributing most to operations.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1958 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: The Service Bureau Corporation → Control Data
deals.description: Sold to Control Data Corporation for approximately $16,000,000 as a principal term of the out-of-court settlement dismissing the CDC antitrust litigation in January 1973. SBC contributed ~$1,500,000 of net earnings on $63,000,000 of gross revenue in 1972 and was consolidated to the January 12 1973 sale date. IBM also agreed not to enter the US data services business for six years.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1972 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: ROLM Corporation
deals.valueNote: 1984 annual report discloses $1,185M in convertible debentures issued for ROLM; total consideration ~$1.3B including cash component
deals.description: Acquired ROLM, a maker of PBX telephone equipment and military computers. IBM sold ROLM to Siemens in 1988 after the business underperformed.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1984 annual report: 'amounts expended for the acquisition of the net assets of ROLM Corporation'

deals.name: ROLM Mil-Spec Computer Division → Loral
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed June 1985. Required by the DOJ consent decree that was a precondition of the IBM/ROLM merger. Acquired by Loral Corporation.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1985 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Copier sales and service operations → Eastman Kodak
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Sold to Eastman Kodak Company to sharpen focus on core computer and communications businesses. Not material to results.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1988 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Science Research Associates → Maxwell Communications
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Wholly owned educational publishing subsidiary sold to Maxwell Communications Corporation. Not material to results.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1988 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: ROLM manufacturing and development → Siemens
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed the sale of ROLM manufacturing and development activities to Siemens AG, closing out the 1984 ROLM acquisition.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1989 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Lexmark International (typewriter & printer business) → Clayton & Dubilier
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Q1 1991 transaction with Clayton & Dubilier created Lexmark International from IBM's former typewriter and office printer business. IBM retained a 10 percent equity interest. Sale of assets net of transaction costs produced no material gain.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1991 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Federal Systems Company → Loral
deals.description: Sale of FSC to Loral Corporation for $1.503 billion in cash. Closing date March 1 1994, effective January 1 1994. Net assets were held for sale at year-end 1993.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1995 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Lotus Development Corporation
deals.valueNote: 1995 cash flow statement: 'Acquisition of Lotus Development Corporation - net (2,880)'
deals.description: Acquired Lotus for its Notes collaboration platform, which became IBM's foundation for enterprise messaging and collaboration software.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1995 cash flow statement direct line item

deals.name: Tivoli Systems, Inc.
deals.valueNote: 1996 cash flow statement: 'Acquisition of Tivoli Systems, Inc. - net (716)'
deals.description: Acquired Tivoli to build IBM's systems management and IT operations software portfolio, now a core part of IBM Automation.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1996 cash flow statement direct line item

deals.name: Global Network → AT&T
deals.description: Completed the sale of the Global Network business to AT&T for $4,991 million. Produced an after-tax benefit of $750 million ($0.40 per diluted share). Removed roughly 2 points of revenue growth.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1999 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Sequent Computer Systems
deals.valueNote: Acquisition announced and closed July 1999; press release cited ~$810M
deals.description: Acquired Sequent for its NUMA (non-uniform memory access) parallel server technology, strengthening IBM's high-end UNIX server line.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1999 CEO letter: 'Sequent Computer Systems strengthens the high end of our Web server line'

deals.name: MiCRUS semiconductor operations → Philips
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Sold MiCRUS semiconductor operations to Philips Semiconductors, an affiliate of Royal Philips Electronics.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2000 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Informix Database Business
deals.valueNote: 2001 CEO letter states '$1.1B for strategic acquisitions' total for the year, with Informix described as 'the bulk'; exact consideration not separately broken out in the note
deals.description: Acquired Informix's database software business from IBM's rival, significantly expanding DB2 market share. The Informix database products were rebranded under the DB2 family.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2001 annual report: 'The bulk of our acquisition investment was used to acquire the database assets of Informix Corp.'

deals.name: Endicott interconnect products operations → Endicott Interconnect Technologies
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Agreement signed Q2 2002, transaction CLOSED in Q4 2002. Recorded a $223 million LOSS on sale in Q2 2002, primarily land, buildings, machinery and equipment, in other (income) and expense. IBM entered a limited supply agreement with EIT and leased back about one third of the Endicott campus. Disclosed as footnote (f) to the 2002 restructuring/special-actions charge table, not in a Divestitures note.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2002 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Hard disk drive (HDD) business → Hitachi
deals.description: Sold the HDD business to Hitachi Ltd for approximately $2 billion; $1,170 million net cash received in 2002. Reported as discontinued operations.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2003 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Mylex → LSI Logic
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Transaction COMPLETED August 2002. Recorded a $74 million LOSS in other (income) and expense. Part of the Microelectronics strategic realignment. Disclosed as footnote (g) to the 2002 restructuring/special-actions charge table, not in a Divestitures note.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2002 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: PricewaterhouseCoopers Consulting
deals.valueNote: Widely reported at $3.5B; closed October 2002. Filing references deal but annual note does not break out final consideration separately.
deals.description: Acquired PwC's consulting arm — 30,000 consultants — instantly creating one of the world's largest IT services businesses. Foundation of what is now IBM Consulting, generating $21B+ annually.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2003 CEO letter: 'PricewaterhouseCoopers Consulting, Rational software and 19 other companies in the past two years'

deals.name: Wireless phone chipset operations → TriQuint Semiconductor
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Sold part of the wireless phone chipset operations to TriQuint Semiconductor Inc in June 2002. Recorded a realized GAIN of $11 million in other (income) and expense. Disclosed as footnote (g) to the 2002 restructuring/special-actions charge table, not in a Divestitures note.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2002 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Rational Software
deals.valueNote: Closed February 2003; widely reported at $2.1B
deals.description: Acquired Rational for its software development tools (UML, requirements management, testing). Now IBM Engineering Lifecycle Management (ELM), used in aerospace, defense, and automotive.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2003 CEO letter reference

deals.name: PC Division → Lenovo
deals.valueNote: 2007 Acquisitions note: 'total consideration agreed to on December 7, 2004 was $1,750 million which included $650 million in cash, $600 million in Lenovo equity and $500 million in assumed liabilities'
deals.description: Sold the ThinkPad PC business to China's Lenovo for $1.75B. IBM retained an 18.9% stake in Lenovo. Strategic exit from commoditizing PC hardware to refocus on higher-margin enterprise technology.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2007 Acquisitions & Divestitures note — prior-year disclosure

deals.name: DataMirror Corporation
deals.valueNote: 2007 Acquisitions note: 'total consideration the company agreed to on January 24, 2007 was $725 million which was paid in cash'
deals.description: Acquired DataMirror for its real-time data replication and integration technology, enhancing IBM's data management portfolio.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2007 Acquisitions & Divestitures note

deals.name: Printing Systems / InfoPrint Solutions (51%) → Ricoh
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Divested 51 percent of its interest in InfoPrint to Ricoh on June 1 2007, forming the InfoPrint Solutions joint venture. IBM continued to provide services to InfoPrint, contributing 4 points of services growth.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2007 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Cognos Inc.
deals.valueNote: 2008 Acquisitions note: 'acquired 100 percent of the outstanding common shares of Cognos for consideration of $5,021 million consisting of $4,998 million of cash and $24 million of equity instruments'
deals.description: Acquired the world's leading business intelligence and performance management software company. Became the foundation of IBM Cognos Analytics, now part of IBM's AI & Analytics portfolio.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2008 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note E)

deals.name: Core logistics operations → Geodis
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed the sale of certain processes, resources, assets and third-party contracts related to core logistics operations to Geodis. Recognized a $298 million gain in Q1 2009.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2009 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: SPSS Inc.
deals.valueNote: Closed October 2009; widely reported at $1.2B. Filing confirms acquisition but exact consideration not captured in this extraction pass.
deals.description: Acquired SPSS, the leading statistical analysis software used in academia, government, and business research. Now IBM SPSS Statistics.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2009 CEO letter reference to SPSS acquisition

deals.name: UniData and UniVerse → Rocket Software
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed October 1 2009. Sold UniData and UniVerse software products and related tools to Rocket Software.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2009 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Dassault PLM sales and support activities → Dassault Systèmes
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed March 31 2010. Sold the activities associated with sales and support of Dassault Systèmes' PLM software, including customer contracts and related assets, back to Dassault.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2010 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: iCluster → Rocket Software
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed the divestiture of the iCluster business to Rocket Software in Q4 2011.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2011 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Retail Store Solutions → Toshiba TEC
deals.description: Definitive agreement announced April 17 2012. Transaction price $850 million with approximately $800 million in cash. Through Dec 31 2012 the first three phases closed: $546 million net proceeds, $251 million note receivable, $446 million net pre-tax gain. Included a multi-year business partner agreement for Smarter Commerce.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2012 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: ACG (Applicazioni Contabili Gestionali) → TeamSystem
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q4 2013. Purchased by TeamSystem. ACG is an Italian ERP solution for small and medium-sized companies. Financial terms not material.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2014 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Cognos Application Development Tools (ADT) → UNICOM Systems
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q4 2013. Purchased by UNICOM Systems Inc. The Cognos ADT suite is a legacy family of COBOL application development environments. Financial terms not material.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2014 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Showcase Reporting → HelpSystems
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q1 2013. Sold the Showcase Reporting product set (acquired via SPSS in 2009) to HelpSystems.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2014 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: SoftLayer Technologies
deals.valueNote: 2013 Acquisitions note: 'completed the acquisition of 100 percent of the privately held company, SoftLayer, a cloud computing infrastructure provider…for cash consideration of $1,977 million'
deals.description: Acquired SoftLayer, a cloud computing infrastructure provider, to establish IBM's global cloud delivery platform. Became the foundation of IBM Cloud.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2013 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note E)

deals.name: Cognos Finance → UNICOM Systems
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed August 31 2014.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Customer care BPO services → SYNNEX
deals.description: Definitive agreement for the worldwide customer care business process outsourcing services business for $501 million: ~$430 million cash plus $71 million in SYNNEX stock (<5% equity). Initial closing Jan 31 2014 with subsequent closings through 2014. Full-year pre-tax gain of $202 million. Concentrix became an IBM strategic business partner.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2014 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Focal Point and PurifyPlus → UNICOM Systems
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q4 2014.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: ILOG JViews and Elixir Visualization → Rogue Wave Software
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q3 2014.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: IMS Tools Suite → Rocket Software
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q3 2014.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Industry standard servers (System x) → Lenovo
deals.description: Announced Jan 23 2014, initial closing Oct 1 2014. Adjusted purchase price $2.1 billion: ~$1.8 billion cash plus Lenovo stock (<5% equity). Covered System x, BladeCenter and Flex System blade servers and switches, x86-based Flex integrated systems, NeXtScale and iDataPlex servers, blade networking and maintenance operations.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2014 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Sterling Transportation Management System → Kewill
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q3 2014.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Algorithmics Collateral Management → SmartStream
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q1 2015.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Kenexa Compensation Portfolio → SCMC Acquisition
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q4 2015.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Merge Healthcare
deals.valueNote: Closed October 2015; widely reported at ~$1B
deals.description: Acquired Merge Healthcare for its medical imaging and clinical data management capabilities, strengthening IBM Watson Health.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2016 annual report reference: 'Merge Healthcare in 2015'

deals.name: Microelectronics → GLOBALFOUNDRIES
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Announced Oct 20 2014, closed July 1 2015. GLOBALFOUNDRIES acquired the Microelectronics business including semiconductor manufacturing in East Fishkill NY and Essex Junction VT. Negative-consideration exit: IBM recorded a $4,726 million pre-tax loss on disposal and a $3,729 million net loss from discontinued operations in 2014. Included a 10-year exclusive manufacturing sourcing agreement for server processor semiconductor technology.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Telecom Expense Management → Tangoe
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q2 2015.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Travel & Transportation kiosk business → Embross North America
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed Q2 2015.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2015 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Truven Health Analytics
deals.valueNote: 2016 Acquisitions note: 'completed the acquisition of 100 percent of Truven…for cash consideration of $2,612 million'
deals.description: Acquired Truven Health Analytics, a leading provider of healthcare data and analytics, for Watson Health. One of IBM's largest healthcare investments.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2016 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note F)

deals.name: Red Hat, Inc.
deals.valueNote: 2019 Acquisitions note: 'the Company completed its acquisition of Red Hat, Inc. for total consideration of $35.1 billion'
deals.description: IBM's largest acquisition ever — the largest software acquisition in history at the time. Red Hat's open-source hybrid cloud platform became IBM's defining strategic bet under Arvind Krishna, who led the deal as SVP of Cloud.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2019 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note E): 'total consideration of $35.1 billion'

deals.name: Select software products (Notes/Domino/Unica/BigFix etc.) → HCL Technologies
deals.description: Announced Dec 6 2018, closed June 30 2019. HCL acquired select standalone Cloud & Cognitive Software products for $1,775 million inclusive of $150 million contingent consideration. In-scope: AppScan, BigFix, Unica, Commerce, Portal, Notes, Domino and Connections. Total pre-tax gain recognized as of Dec 31 2020 was $669 million.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2020 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Kyndryl Spin-off
deals.valueNote: Kyndryl's market cap at separation on November 3, 2021 was approximately $19B. No cash consideration — IBM distributed Kyndryl shares to IBM shareholders in a tax-free spinoff.
deals.description: Spun off IBM's managed infrastructure services business as an independent public company (NYSE: KD). IBM's largest-ever divestiture by revenue — Kyndryl had ~$19B in annual revenue at separation. The spinoff allowed IBM to refocus entirely on hybrid cloud and AI.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2021 annual report: 'the separation of Kyndryl that occurred on November 3, 2021'

deals.name: OEM commercial financing capabilities
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Q3 2021. Sale of the company's remaining OEM commercial financing capabilities reported within the Financing segment. Agreement entered Q4 2020. Financial terms not material.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2021 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Healthcare software assets (Watson Health) → Francisco Partners
deals.description: Signed January 2022, US/Canada closed June 30 2022, most other countries in 2H 2022, final country closings in 2023. $1,065 million. Assets: Health Insights, MarketScan, Clinical Development, Social Program Management, Micromedex and imaging software. Total pre-tax gain as of Dec 31 2023 was $303 million.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2023 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: Apptio (from Vista Equity Partners)
deals.valueNote: Closed August 2023; IBM press release cited ~$4.6B
deals.description: Acquired Apptio, the leading Technology Business Management (TBM) and FinOps software platform, to help enterprises optimize technology spending. IBM's largest acquisition since Red Hat.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2023 annual report: 'Apptio acquisition' referenced in cash flow discussion

deals.name: QRadar SaaS assets → Palo Alto Networks
deals.valueNote: IBM disclosed no sale price for this transaction.
deals.description: Completed August 31 2024. Sold certain QRadar SaaS assets including QRadar intellectual property, customer relationships and customer contracts to Palo Alto Networks, alongside a partnership to deliver AI-powered security using watsonx. IBM is facilitating migration of QRadar SaaS and on-prem clients to Palo Alto's Cortex XSIAM.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2024 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: StreamSets & webMethods (from Software AG)
deals.valueNote: 2024 annual report: 'completed the acquisition of StreamSets and webMethods from Software AG…$2.3 billion'
deals.description: Acquired Software AG's data integration and API management platforms, strengthening IBM's hybrid integration portfolio for AI-ready data pipelines.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2024 annual report: 'acquisition of StreamSets and webMethods from Software AG…$2.3 billion'

deals.name: The Weather Company assets → Francisco Partners
deals.description: Signed August 2023, closed January 31 2024 to Zephyr Buyer L.P. (Francisco Partners). Headline $1,100 million inclusive of $250 million contingent consideration; $750 million cash at closing plus a $100 million 7-year seller-financing loan. Pre-tax gain ~$240 million. Closes the loop on the 2016 Weather Company acquisition.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2024 annual report — Acquisitions & Divestitures / filing text

deals.name: HashiCorp
deals.valueNote: 2025 Acquisitions note: 'Total consideration $7,433' (millions)
deals.description: Acquired HashiCorp, the leading multi-cloud infrastructure automation platform (Terraform, Vault, Consul). Extends IBM's hybrid cloud platform with best-in-class infrastructure-as-code capabilities.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2025 Acquisitions & Divestitures note: 'Total consideration $7,433 million'

deals.name: Confluent, Inc.
deals.valueNote: 2026 Q1 10-Q Note 5: 'Total consideration $11,590' (millions); $31.00/share cash, ~$11.3B equity value
deals.description: Acquired Confluent, the data-streaming platform built on Apache Kafka, to strengthen real-time data flow for generative and agentic AI across applications and APIs. Integrated into the Software segment.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2026 Q1 10-Q, Note 5 (Acquisitions & Divestitures): 'On March 17, 2026, the company completed the acquisition of all of the outstanding shares of Confluent ... Total consideration $11,590 million'

annualSummary._comment: Aggregate M&A spend per year from CEO letters/MD&A (where IBM discloses total acquisition spending). Captures the many smaller deals ($50-500M) not individually listed above.

2002.note: CEO letter: 'PwC Consulting, Rational software and 19 other companies'
